correctness.rationale: The conditional distribution of G(n,m) after marking an isolated vertex is exactly G(n-1,m); connected induced copies cannot use that vertex. This yields a hypergeometric mixed-moment ratio; finite-factor monotonicity and zero boundary give at most one sign reversal. Inclusion–exclusion gives the n>=2k-2 onset; fixed-product asymptotics give p*=(2h-k)/(k(k-2)). Complete motifs and G(n,p) boundaries are treated separately. Independently enumerated exact covariances for all n<=6 across seven connected motifs agree, and 5,483 exact checker assertions passed. Finite checks are not taken as infinite proof.

General hypergeometric moment methods could yield a derivation, which remains a residual priority risk.

evidence: The tree-component formula counts connected components that are trees; such copies must have all external edges absent, whereas an induced tree is defined only by its internal edges. Their conditional hypergeometric event probabilities and edge supports differ.
The induced triangle–open-triad formula concerns covariance of two 3-vertex motif counts and does not include total isolated vertices.

The examined published works prove distributional approximations or directed-path correlations, not the normalized exact identity, monotone sign ratio, or universal asymptotic density for connected induced H.

originality.rationale: Searched published mathematical records, recoverable prior scientific claims, exact-moment aliases, and primary literature. The closest same-model prior computation involves tree COMPONENT counts, whereas the new count is induced copies with unrestricted exterior edges and all connected motif edge densities. Sah–Sawhney proves local limits, Reinert–Röllin gives independent-edge covariance matrices, and Alm–Janson–Linusson handles oriented connectivity events. No inspected result implies the exact shape-independent mixed covariance and one-switch/dense thresholds. This is a best-knowledge judgment, not external priority certification.
residual_risks: An older exact multivariate generating-function or hypergeometric overlap identity for G(n,m) might implicitly imply the covariance without the same terminology.
The tree-component one-switch classification is closely related but not logically dominating; it warrants careful priority scrutiny for conceptual proximity.
The exact sign phase at constant edge density concerns exponentially rare isolated vertices; it is not a macroscopic covariance or critical-window theorem.
Historical priority and the mathematical proof have not been independently audited.

value.rationale: The connected induced motif/isolation pair probes clustering under a fixed edge budget. This theorem classifies all connected motif types simultaneously through k and h, proves a strict single-transition law and a uniform finite sample onset, and derives the universal induced-tree asymptotic threshold p=1/k. The independent-edge model has the opposite all-negative sign and exposes the structural effect of conditioning on the edge budget. This is more than an ad hoc parameter slice or a table entry.
